leads.claim: When a host writes a child's input before it reads the child's exit, write it inside the scope that reaps the child and treat a closed or reset pipe as no error, because a child that refuses at startup exits unread and a large input then turns its classified exit and stderr into an unreaped broken-pipe exception.
leads.because: athena-portable 3ef59b4: a 4 MiB stdin to a child that exits 2 without reading raised BrokenPipeError (WinError 109) out of the transport, skipping ADR 0109's exit classification and leaving the child unreaped; after the fix the exit code and stderr tail are reported. No subprocess-lifecycle technique mentions stdin or a broken pipe.
